scope: CP24 runner correctness and synthetic validation only; not a compiler acceptance or performance verdict
findings: Default and legacy missing query_cache field produce byte-for-byte parent argv across both arms, check/build phases, and object-cache settings.

Explicit query_cache=true adds the same option and per-sequence cache subdirectory in both arms; execute creates a distinct fresh work directory per sequence and retains it across exactly four requests.
prepare freezes the option without modifying request/case weights, ABBA ordering, estimators or schema identifier.

validate_rows binds query/parse excerpts to raw JSON and raw log hashes whenever query_cache is enabled; explicit query requested=true is required even after rehashing a changed raw report and updating its excerpt.
Independent controls reject query excerpt changes, parse excerpt changes, raw report edits, missing/wrong-type query report, integer requested=1, removed argv flag and changed cache path.
The same validation is reused by checked_preflight and summarize; failures suppress scores in the independently rerun suite.

Legacy schema/2 rows missing the new report excerpts validate under the false/missing flag. A historical plan must still use its original runner hash; changing to this runner does not bypass that existing freeze contract.
nonblocking_limits: A matching requested=true report with state=bypass is intentionally accepted, and parse_cache may be absent to support older baseline binaries. A successful runner result alone does not establish actual CP22 cache engagement or hits; inspect raw report states and hit/miss counts in the real CLI window.
These 18 additional controls use synthetic reports and the author test fixture; they do not execute a compiler or establish timing results.
The raw-log/excerpt hash binding detects disagreement and retained-evidence mutation, not malicious wholesale re-creation of a plan, records, logs and receipts.
